misconceptions.description: Writing resume bullets that list responsibilities or vague traits instead of a concrete artifact and a measurable result
misconceptions.trigger: learner writes Responsible for spreadsheets or Hard worker as evidence
misconceptions.feedback: Replace duty statements with artifact plus result: what you built, the skill it shows, and a number or outcome a reader can picture.

misconceptions.description: Inflating skill level on a resume (expert, mastered) beyond what the actual experience supports
misconceptions.trigger: learner labels an introductory experience as expert or mastery
misconceptions.feedback: State the true scope: the course you took and the concrete thing you made. Honest framing survives the first interview question; inflation does not.

misconceptions.description: Keeping an AI-invented accomplishment on a resume because it sounds impressive, even though it never happened
misconceptions.trigger: learner retains a fabricated bullet generated by an AI rewrite
misconceptions.feedback: You are accountable for every claim. Delete anything you cannot back with real evidence, and disclose that AI helped with wording, not facts.

misconceptions.description: Submitting one untailored resume for every posting instead of surfacing the evidence the specific role asks for
misconceptions.trigger: learner leaves unrelated bullets at the top and ignores the posting's named skills
misconceptions.feedback: Tailor to the posting: promote the bullets that match its required skills and trim the rest. Role fit beats length or decoration.

misconceptions.description: Treating a screenshot or a bare claim as sufficient portfolio evidence when the live published URL is the strongest, checkable evidence.
misconceptions.trigger: portfolio lists 'Built a website' with no link, or shows only a screenshot of the page
misconceptions.feedback: A reviewer trusts what they can open. Link the live URL and name what the artifact shows ('my CAT 100 data story, published at <URL>, with a working evidence link'); a screenshot can rot quietly and a claim cannot be checked at all.
